title: Federal award reporting: 2 CFR 200 performance reports, prior approvals and agency report formats
authority: Office of Management and Budget (2 CFR Part 200); NIH; NSF

provenance.source: 2 CFR 200.308, 200.328 and 200.329 (eCFR, current as of 2026-10-07; sections last amended 2024-10-01); NIH RPPR reporting requirements; NSF project reporting
provenance.license: Paraphrased summary (source: public domain US government)

verifyNote: Verify before relying: the award's terms and conditions set the report format and due dates and override these defaults. Foundations set their own formats.

items.title: Accomplishments compared with the award's objectives
items.text: As applicable, a performance report compares accomplishments with the objectives the award set for the reporting period, explains why established goals or objectives were not met, and explains cost overruns or higher-than-expected unit costs.

items.title: Relate financial data and accomplishments to the goals
items.text: When reporting performance, the recipient relates financial data and accomplishments to the performance goals and objectives of the award, and gives cost information (such as unit costs) when the award's terms require it. For discretionary research awards this may be limited to technical performance reports. Agencies use OMB-approved common forms such as the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR).

items.title: How often performance reports are due
items.text: Performance reports are due as the award requires, no less often than annually and no more often than quarterly unless specific conditions apply.

items.title: Annual performance report: federal default
items.text: An annual report is due no later than 90 calendar days after the reporting period, unless the agency requires annual reports before the anniversary dates of a multi-year award (as NIH and NSF do).

items.title: Quarterly or semiannual performance report
items.text: A quarterly or semiannual report is due no later than 30 calendar days after the reporting period.

items.title: Final performance report
items.text: The recipient's final performance report is due no later than 120 calendar days after the period of performance ends (90 days for a subrecipient reporting to a pass-through entity). The agency may extend a due date with justification.

items.title: Significant developments between reports
items.text: Problems, delays or adverse conditions that will affect milestones or objectives, and developments that allow meeting them sooner, at lower cost or with different beneficial results, are reported to the agency when they occur. A negative development comes with a corrective action plan and any help needed.

items.title: Financial reports
items.text: Financial reporting uses OMB-approved data elements (currently the SF-425), at least annually and at most quarterly. Annual financial reports are due within 90 calendar days of the period, quarterly or semiannual within 30, and the final within 120 days of the end of the period of performance. Numbers in the performance report should agree with them.

items.title: Deviations reported, prior approval requested
items.text: Deviations from the approved budget, scope or objectives are reported in the performance report, and the revisions that need prior approval are requested from the agency or pass-through entity.

items.title: Prior approval: change in scope or objective
items.text: A change in the scope or objective of the project needs prior written approval, even with no budget change.

items.title: Prior approval: key personnel and PI effort
items.text: A change in key personnel named in the award needs prior written approval, as does the PI's disengagement for more than three months or a 25 percent reduction in the PI's time and effort over the period of performance.

items.title: Prior approval: budget changes
items.text: Prior written approval is also needed to move participant support funds to other categories, to add subaward work not in the approved application, to change the approved cost-sharing amount, for additional federal funds, and to move funds between construction and non-construction work. Agencies may restrict transfers among direct cost categories over 10 percent of the total budget on awards above the simplified acquisition threshold.

items.title: No-cost extensions
items.text: Where the award allows, a recipient may start a one-time extension of up to 12 months by notifying the agency in writing at least 10 calendar days before the period ends; it needs prior approval when the terms prohibit it, it needs more federal funds, or it changes the approved scope. Other no-cost extensions need prior approval, requested at least 10 calendar days before the end.

items.title: NIH: Research Performance Progress Report
items.text: NIH uses the RPPR. Annual SNAP RPPRs are due about 45 days before the next budget period starts, non-SNAP about 60 days before, and multi-year funded RPPRs annually on or before the anniversary; the final RPPR is due 120 days after the end of the period of performance. Check exact dates in eRA Commons.

items.title: NSF: annual, final and project outcomes reports
items.text: NSF annual project reports are due no later than 90 days before the end of the current budget period and are submitted in Research.gov. The final annual report covers only the last year and is due within 120 days of the award's end date, as is the Project Outcomes Report: no more than 800 words, for a public audience, posted as submitted.
